en: (That only got her more worked up.)
(Once she's said her piece, she'll calm down and pay for the ride, I'm sure. I'll just stay quiet and listen.)
Too many taxi drivers treat their passengers like imbeciles! Don't they give you training? I highly doubt it!
You have no professionalism at all! You've got to remember, this is a service industry!
(Seems she's just getting warmed up.)
And these days we get drivers who don't even know the roads, or who drive like maniacs!
It's true! I read it in a weekly magazine! Manners and morals among taxi drivers have taken a dive!
(Now she's not even talking about her own complaints against me.)
I also saw that some of you guys used to be presidents of failed companies! What's the world coming to!?
You work hard all your life, then one mistake and you're out on the curb, your wife and child leaving you by the roadside. What a miserable time!
Kids these days have their hopes and dreams crushed before they even get out of school! Who's responsible for this mess!?
(What is she even complaining about now?)
*pant* *pant* It feels good to get that off my chest. Let me out here.
(She seems to have calmed down, but that monologue was exhausting.)
Sorry I grumped the whole way. I probably took it a bit too far.
Here is the fare. And I think you deserve a tip for hearing me out, too.
I appreciate the service you gave me, driver. I think I'll be in a better mood next time.
Phew. We made it. Here's the fare.
I feel better now that I got all that out of my system. This makes for great stress relief.
This is the worst ride I've ever had. It's ridiculous that I even have to pay for it!
I wanted to relieve my stress by getting some complaints off my chest, but now I'm more stressed than ever! I hope I never see you again!
(I wasn't able to give her good service. This was one tiring ride. Taxi driving is tough.)
Hey, driver. I wanna go to <Color:22>Getto Hot Spring<Color:Default>. Ya know it?
(Sounds like she's from Kansai, not a local.)
Yes, I know it. Let's go.
What route would you like to go?
I ain't from 'round here, dolt! How the hell am I s'posed to know the way!?
I'll leave it to you. Just get us there however's best. I'm gonna have myself a little nap!
(So the route is up to me, huh?)
(She'll never know if I take the long way.)
(She woke up...)
How long till we get there?
About thirty minutes.
What!? That can't be right! I heard it only takes about fifteen!
But you said you'd leave it up to⑬
Idiot! I meant I'd leave figurin' out the shortest route to you!
Who'd wanna spend any longer with you than they have to!? Take the quickest route!
Okay, sorry about that.
(She's asleep, but taking the shortest route would be the best idea.)
Where are we now?
<Color:22>Chikuzengawa Street<Color:Default>.
Idiot! I ain't know the roads 'round here!
Ya sure this <Color:22>Chikuzengawa Street<Color:Default> is the quickest way to go?
Heh! Bet you're thinkin' you can rip me off just 'cause I'm not from 'round here!
No, this is definitely the shortest route. You can check it on the map if you'd like.
Hmph. Never mind. If you insist, I'll have to trust ya. Just don't go gettin' in any accidents.
I'll be careful.
(It seems like she believed me. I should have confirmed the route in advance given that she doesn't know the lay of the land.)
(It'd be best to confirm the route with her.)
What!? I'm tryin' to sleep here!
I just wanted to confirm the route with you. <Color:22>Nagasu Boulevard<Color:Default> is the most direct way there.
But at this time of day it's pretty congested. I think we should take <Color:22>Chikuzengawa Street<Color:Default> instead.
Would you like to check on the map?
Nah, you seem like the trustworthy type. That'll be fine!
Thank you. We should be there in fifteen minutes.
When ya don't know a place, it's easy to get ripped off. I'm glad you're so thorough, driver!
All righty, let's go!
Hrm, I'm not sleepy anymore. Got any news to share, driver?
What sort of things are you interested in?
Current events, ya know? That sorta thing.
Current events, huh?
Okay, well how about some political discussion?
Sure. Whaddya think of the current rulin' party, driver?
Well, I don't support all their policies...
And why the hell not!?
I'm a member of the National Women's Association for that party. That's why I'm here in Fukuoka!
What is it ya can't support!? Go on, spit it out! I'll tell ya exactly how wrong you are!
Heheh, got ya! I was only jokin'. Politics bore me to death, actually.
You oughta know that politics, religion, and war are tricky subjects to bring up to someone ya just met.
It ain't good to discuss sensitive subjects when you're in the service industry, driver.
(She's right. Who is this lady?)
Okay, how about a dirty joke?
What!? I ain't your drinkin' buddy, pal! I'm a passenger! And a woman at that!
How's a dirty joke a current event, anyway?
You better watch what ya say when dealin' with customers. Dirty jokes are a no-no.
And that's not all. You should stay away from politics, religion, and war as well.
Well, how about we talk some sports?
Ah, good choice. You like baseball? I guess if you're from Fukuoka you'd⑬
I actually lived in Tokyo the longest.
Then I guess you're a Tokyo Gigants fan? I'm Osaka born and bred, which makes us arch rivals!
Our team'll show the Gigants how it's done next season, mark my words! It'll be a legendary showdown!
(That seemed to spark her interest.)
Sports was the right thing to go with, driver. There's all sorts of topics out there, but ya can't just go sayin' whatever ya like.
It ain't good to discuss sensitive subjects when you're in the service industry. And that goes double for dirty jokes.
We're almost there, ma'am.
Ah, great! Mind if I pay with a 10,000 yen note?
(I've taken a lot of big notes today, so I don't think I'll have enough change for that.)
I'm very sorry. I don't seem to have enough change on me.
You wouldn't happen to have anything smaller?
Nope! All I got is 10,000 yen notes!
You could also pay by credit card.
Nah. Never liked the things, so I don't carry one. Surely you can make a 10,000 yen note work.
Look! There's a convenience store over there!
I'll park in front of the convenience store.
Can I ask you to go in and get some change?
What? Ya want me to go!? The passenger!?
I'll turn the meter off, of course.
That ain't the problem, driver.
I know I don't have any small bills on me either, but keepin' enough change on hand is your job.
But sometimes ya run out of money to make change. It happens.
How ya deal with that when it happens is the important part.
And if ya do it right, you can turn the inconvenience into a positive impression.
I'm sorry. I'll go in and get change myself.
Yeah, you do that.
Is there anything you'd like me to buy while I'm in there?
Hey, that's the way! Doin' somethin' thoughtful like that leaves a good impression. Can ya buy me a can of coffee, then?
(She looks like a typical passenger, but she seems well-versed in service skills.)
I'm sorry about this, but would you mind waiting while I go in to the convenience store to get some change?
Oh, not at all. I'll be right here.
Do you drink tea or coffee?
I'm a coffee drinker. Why?
Well, I need to buy something to get change, so I thought I could get you a drink to make up for the inconvenience.
Oh, that's very kind of ya, driver!
It was my fault I ran out of change.
Still, everybody makes mistakes.
The important part is how ya handle them.
And how ya handled that just now completely made up for the whole thing. I'd even say it gives a better impression. Top marks for service!
(I seem to have handled that the right way.)
Excuse me, ma'am.
Well, I was just thinking, some of my passengers like to leave me the change as a tip.
And?
If you gave me the change from this 10,000 yen note as a tip, you wouldn't need any money back.
If I was in Osaka, I'd think you were makin' a joke. But you're dead serious, aren't ya!?
Ya moron! You're the one who ran out of change, right!?
It's only natural to make mistakes, but what's important is how ya deal with those mistakes.
The service industry is funny in that, dependin' on how ya handle a mistake, it can turn a negative experience into a positive one.
But you chose the absolute worst solution! Ya need to think about your customers more!
I'm sorry. I'll go and get some change in the convenience store.
Yeah, you do that. And don't forget to stop the meter!
Thank you very much. Your service skills were excellent.
(Huh? Her Kansai accent is gone.)
I'm actually an undercover examiner, testing the service given by taxi drivers.
An undercover examiner?
You gave me exceptional service today, Suzuki-san. I'll be sure to pass that on to Nakajima-san.
This is the fare, and a tip from your boss. He wanted me to give it to those who did well.
Keep up the good work.
Thank you. Your service skills are quite good.
You gave me good service today, Suzuki-san. I'll pass that on to Nakajima-san.
Here is the fare.
You need to take the service side of your job a little more seriously, Suzuki-san.
I'm not looking forward to telling Nakajima-san about your results.
Oh. I'm sorry about today.
Yes, well, keep working on it.
<Color:22>Chikuzengawa Street<Color:Default>, and step on it!
And no detours, aight? The shortest, quickest route.
(They've got a bit of an attitude.)
Man, I'm getting jittery. Got a smoke on you?
Yeah, I got it.

en: Give me one. I'm all out.
I'm afraid this is a nonsmoking taxi.
Shut the fuck up and drive!
(They're pretty full of themselves.)
(I don't like it, but it'd get ugly otherwise.)
Okay, I'll let you smoke just this once.
Geez, man! Why didn't you say so to start with!?
He's just a taxi driver. Not much they can do if a customer pushes for something.
(They're getting a little too confident. I guess I shouldn't have given them permission.)
Give me that smoke.
Sure... Huh? Oh, looks like I forgot my cigs at home today.
Shit, now you tell me!
I'll pick some up as soon as we get out.
Sorry, but I'll have to ask to you to refrain from smoking in here.
Hey, we're the customers here, driver!
Yeah, the customer comes first!
Indeed, you're both valued customers.
But many of my other customers dislike the smell of cigarette smoke.
I smoke myself, so I know how you feel. But please, hold on for just a bit longer.
Tch. Fine.
You better get us where we're going quick!
Thank you for your patience.
(That seems to have worked.)
Gah, I'm really dying for a cig!
The longer you go without, the more you want it, huh? I'm getting the shakes myself.
I'm talking to you, idiot! Talk to us about something to distract us!
I'm not really the chatty type.
Aren't you a taxi driver!? What do you think we're payin' you for?
If driving's all there was to it, I could do your job for you, loser!
(These guys are a pain in the neck. How am I going to deal with this?)
Have you drove a taxi before?
'Course not! Who'd want to drive an old hunk of junk like this!?
But he does drifting up on the mountain roads, so driving a taxi would be a piece of cake!
Have you ever had your family ride along?
Nah, I'm single right now.
Try driving with your loved ones on board. It's much trickier than drifting, I promise you.
Our passengers are more important than anything.
Ensuring they get to their destination safely may sound simple, but it's a challenging job.
Man, you're boring us to tears here! Just stop talking and get us where we need to go, quick!
(I think they understood my point, at least.)
(They're bullies, but I don't want any trouble.)
I'm sorry that I'm not better at conversation.
You should be! Your service sucks, dude!
Bet you haven't even been doing this long. You got fired from your last job, didn't you?
Hahah. I reckon your days are numbered in this job, too. You can't do anything!
(They're really sticking the knives in. I shouldn't have tried the apology route.)
We're almost there.
Forget the fare. This is as far as you go.
What!? Are you kidding me? We're your passengers here!
Passengers need to show some manners when riding in my taxi. No manners, no ride.
Who the hell do you think you are!?
Fine, we'll get out. But you're getting out with us, driver!
Yeah, hurry it up!
Gah! Is this guy made of stone!?
Who the hell are you!?
